content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text rules a dispute UNDERDETERMINED and gives a reason, so K-S2's restriction on grounds for UNDERDETERMINED is in issue.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED' — read narrowly as barring only rulings that rest on a single verse's silence, or broadly as barring any underdetermination in a verse-based dispute.","why":"The judge's stated ground is that two chains do not force each other, not that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary."}
